page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing and database performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU stress tests, software compilation, and database operations, alongside high static web serving throughput. Cryptographic operations benefit from hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. Memory bandwidth and single-core performance sit in the average range, though the system demonstrates strong text generation speeds during small-scale language model inference.

Given its massive memory footprint, dedicated CPU allocation, and high-speed local NVMe storage, the x2idn.16xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require large in-memory datasets without the overhead of external storage latency. This instance is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory analytics, enterprise resource planning systems, and heavy data processing pipelines.
